name: LGD-4033 cycle

lead: LGD-4033, also sold as Ligandrol, is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and later licensed to Viking Therapeutics. Users run it in defined courses called cycles, usually bundled with other products, hoping to gain muscle mass and strength for a larger, leaner look.

Early trials found lean mass gains in healthy men and in people recovering from hip fracture. The same trials and later reports found it lowers testosterone, and regulators have not approved it for any use.

paras: Forum discussions describe courses of several weeks taken orally, often paired with testosterone-support products, with users comparing plans and tracking bloodwork. Specifics of dosing and sourcing are deliberately not given here.

Studies report reduced testosterone, SHBG and HDL cholesterol; case reports link non-medical use to liver injury. The FDA issued warning letters in 2017 to supplement firms selling it, WADA prohibits it, and many online products contain none of the compound or other substances.

angle.text: Trials show lean mass gains with LGD-4033, and users take courses of it for a larger, leaner physique. The same trials show hormone suppression.

lead: An LGD-4033 cycle is a planned multi-week course of LGD-4033 (Ligandrol), an investigational nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator, used by lifters in the hope of adding lean muscle and strength [1]. A looksmax.org thread shows members planning an eight-week first course and comparing add-on products to manage suppression [2].

Ligand Pharmaceuticals discovered the compound in 2010 and Viking Therapeutics licensed it in 2014 [1]. Phase 1 trials reported lean mass gains and a phase 2 trial in hip fracture recovery found dose-dependent lean mass gains [1]. It remains unapproved [1].
Community reports are mixed: one T Nation user described feeling run down around week four, and another reported total testosterone falling from 642 to 432 after about four and a half weeks [3][4].

paras: A cycle refers to a bounded period of use followed by a break, borrowed from anabolic steroid culture. The looksmax.org thread shows a first-time user planning an eight-week course and asking others to review it, and replies suggest changes and debate whether recovery measures are needed [2].

Per Wikipedia, phase 1 trials in healthy men reported about 1.2 kg lean mass gain over three weeks, and a phase 2 trial of 108 hip fracture patients reported dose-dependent lean mass gains of up to about 9 percent placebo-adjusted [1]. LGD-4033 lowers total and free testosterone, FSH and SHBG and reduces HDL cholesterol, while trials did not show raised liver enzymes though case reports link non-medical use to liver injury [1].
Forum users report suppressed testosterone after use, one citing a drop from 642 to 432 ng/dL with no recovery treatment, and others discuss lipid changes seen in bloodwork [4][5].

LGD-4033 is an Investigational New Drug in the US and not approved [1]. The FDA issued warning letters in 2017 to two companies marketing it as a dietary supplement, and WADA prohibits it, with athletes testing positive across sports [1]. Many products sold online contain none of the compound or other substances [1].

Published phase 1 and phase 2 trials are summarised above; they examined lean mass, strength, safety and hormone levels at doses studied under medical supervision, and use outside trials often exceeds those conditions [1].
